newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parlt approves holding law for TV sector.
newsitem.headline: Italy parlt approves holding law for TV sector.

text.p: The Italian Senate approved a stop-gap decree at the weekend to extend the broadcasting licences of opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset company until the end of next May.

The decree, worked out in a deal between the government and the centre-right Freedom Alliance bloc ahead of full legislation for the television sector, was earlier ratified by the lower house of parliament and now becomes law.
It replaces an expiring decree which gave Mediaset the right to carry on operating its three terrestrial television channels until the end of January.

Mediaset's licences will now be allowed to run for a further four months and they could be extended to the end of July if one of the two houses of parliament approves full legislation on the television sector by May.
The Constitutional Court ruled two years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels and set August 1996 as the deadline for changes to be implemented.

The government extended current ownership rules until the end of January 1997 after the deadline passed in order to plug a legal gap under which magistrates could technically have forced Berlusconi to take one of his channels off the air.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi wants to introduce wide-ranging legislation for Italian television by the end of March. The sector is now dominated by Berlusconi's Mediaset stations and the three channels operated by state-owned RAI.
The new decree increased parliament's power over RAI, giving the parliamentary broadcasting committee the right to ask the prime minister to sack the state company's board of governors.
The Senate also pledged to enact a 1995 referendum which called for RAI's eventual privatisation.
